title: Editable cost annotations: inline workflow usability sweep and handoff
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Customers want to attach short, contextual notes to cost spikes and recurring charge lines in the Console so teams can track investigations (e.g., 'autoscaler misconfigured', 'feature flag rollout', 'cache warmup'). Current cost views only support bulk comments in a separate timeline which breaks discoverability. Goal: design an inline, editable annotation UI that is discoverable at glance, minimally obtrusive, keyboard-accessible, and safe for enterprise (audit trail + opt-out). This ticket covers prototype iterations, stakeholder reviews, redlines, and final dev handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Inline annotation affordance appears on hover for cost rows and summary tiles
Clicking affordance opens a lightweight edit field anchored to the row (not full modal)
Annotations support short markdown (bold, code) and are saved with author/time metadata displayed in a micro-summary
All actions are accessible via keyboard (enter to edit, esc to cancel, ctrl+enter to save)
Annotation creation and edits emit telemetry events (annotation.created, annotation.updated) visible in the console telemetry dashboard
Design handoff includes token-level spacing, color tokens for states, and interaction redlines for dev implementation
handoff_notes: Primary recommendation: anchor inline editor under table row with a 320px max width and 12px elevation. Use semantic color token --warning-100 for draft border and --neutral-800 for text. Save flow: optimistic UI update; if server rejects, show inline toast with revert option. Include telemetry event mapping in PRD. Devs should implement simple markdown rendering; escape rich injections. Link to GitHub PR with initial front-end scaffold.
qa_checks: Hover affordance shows within 200ms on desktop and does not block row selection
Keyboard flows covered: focus -> enter -> edit -> ctrl+enter saves
Autosave and rollback behavior under transient network failure tested
Screen reader announces 'annotation, editable' when focused
Audit trail entries visible in activity log for enterprise customers with retention policy
comments: 2025-02-19 - Owen Brooks: Initial wireframes uploaded to Figma. Added two interaction variants (inline popover vs inline expand). Requesting engineering feasibility check on optimistic updates and space within tight table rows.

2025-02-21 - Leila Navarro (PM): Prefer inline popover that doesn't cause reflow. PM note: must not add extra per-row DOM elements for perf; consider virtualized list impact. Link to PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COST/Inline+Annotations+PRD

2025-02-24 - Raj Singh (Engineering): Feasibility: inline popover okay; prefer portal-based anchor to avoid table clipping. Concern: telemetry flood if annotations emit on every keystroke — suggest debounced events and explicit save event. Filed ENG-34122 as dependency.

2025-02-27 - Emma Wu (Design reviewer): Visual redlines attached. Adjusted microcopy: 'Add note' -> 'Annotate' to reduce verbosity. Change action color to subtle-blue instead of yellow for better contrast. See Figma comments for exact tokens.

2025-03-01 - Security (Nina Ford): Confirmed no sensitive data collection. Recommend opt-out for annotation syncing to external analytics for regulated customers. Added label 'security-review-required' and follow-up flow in Confluence.

2025-03-02 - QA (Jordan Park): Ran accessibility sweep on prototype. Found missing aria-label on save button and non-announced toast. Added QA checklist items. Marked minor visual pixel offsets in mobile condensed rows.

2025-03-03 - Owen Brooks: Updated prototype to include keyboard flows and debounce for telemetry. Preparing handoff package. GitHub PR scaffold: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-ui/pull/4231. Moving to In Review.

2025-03-03 - Maya Patel: Quick decision log: chosen inline popover anchored via portal, optimistic UI with 6s undo toast, telemetry events on create/update/delete only. Trade-offs: small increase in bundle size for markdown render library vs better user experience for formatted notes. Noted to revisit if bundle impact > 20KB gzipped.
